article_content: 'Twenty-year-old Thomas Doty tragically lost his battle with a rare bone cancer, Osteosarcoma. His mother, Tiffany, believes a deceptive promise of $250,000 for his treatment may have cost him his life.  After 'Deadliest Catch' star Jonathan Hillstrand, a family friend, rallied support for Thomas, a woman posing as an Indiana nurse contacted the family, pledging a substantial sum.  This false assurance, according to Mrs. Doty, caused critical delays in his surgery.  The family's attorney intends to pursue legal action against the perpetrator if identified.'

Isy, Tiffany, oguerovia peteĩ kuña japu ombohováiva'ekue chupekuéra 250.000 dólares reheve omyañávo imemby pohãnohárape. Jonathan Hillstrand, pe 'Deadliest Catch' pegua ha iñamigo kuéra, ojerure'asy chupekuéra oipytyvõ haguã Thomas-pe. Upéi, peteĩ kuña he'íva Indiana-gua pohãnoháraha oikuaauka chupekuéra ome'ẽtaha pe pirapire. Pe kuña japu ogueroviauka Tiffany-pe ombotapykuehague imemby ñemonguera. Pe abogado he'i ohekátaha pe kuñápe okumpli haguã pe léi.'

article_content: 'On Father's Day morning, a devastating accident claimed the life of Amanda Ezra, a 24-year-old mother from Mishawaka, Indiana. Ezra was riding in a minivan with four others after a night out with friends. Around 5 a.m., while the vehicle was moving along Chestnut Street in Osceola, Ezra leaned out the window to be sick. Tragically, her head struck a telephone pole, resulting in a fatal injury. Police reports indicate that the driver was intoxicated and left the accident scene, but was subsequently taken into custody. Ezra, who leaves behind three children aged between two and eight, was in the process of turning her life around. She had enrolled at a local community college and aspired to be a teacher. A memorial has been established outside her home, where community members have gathered to express their condolences.'

Ezra oho hína peteĩ minivan-pe irundy tapicha ndive, osẽ rire iñirũnguéra ndive pyhare.  5 aravo jave, pe mba'yrumýi Chestnut Street, Osceola-pe ohasárõ guare, Ezra omosẽ akã okẽgui okyhyjégui.  Ivaipa jepémo, iñakã oñorairõ peteĩ poste-pe, ha upéva omohu'ã hekove. Policía he'i pe mba'yrumýi omýiva oka'úhague ha oheja pe accidente, ha upéi ojeapresa chupe. Ezra, ohejava mbohapy imemby mokõi ha poapy áño oguerekóva apytépe, oñeha'ãmbaite omyatyrõ hekove. Oike peteĩ universidad-pe ha oikoségui mbo'ehára. Ojejapo peteĩ ñemomorã hogapýpe, tapichakuéra oñembyatyhápe ohechauka haguã ñembyasy.'

article_content: 'Chick-fil-A expands drone delivery pilot program to Florida. The fast-food chain, known for its bustling drive-thru lanes, initiated testing in Brandon, Florida, last week. This follows earlier tests at locations in Granbury, Texas, and Durham, North Carolina, since September 2022.  Chick-fil-A stated they are in the early stages of testing drone delivery at a limited number of restaurants. In Florida, eligible customers can order via the Chick-fil-A app. Food arrives in a cardboard box, lowered to backyards by a hovering drone using a wire.  The company is partnering with DroneUp, a Virginia Beach-based drone company also working with Walmart. Drone delivery is gaining popularity in the US, with companies like Flytrex, an ultrafast drone delivery service, collaborating with several restaurant chains, including Chick-fil-A in Texas and North Carolina since September 2022.  Beyond drone delivery, Chick-fil-A is testing other autonomous technologies like delivery robots in select California, Texas, and Florida restaurants. In Texas, one restaurant has even employed a robot for dine-in food delivery.'
translated_content: 'Chick-fil-A ombohasa hembi'apu oguejy reko yvágare Florida-pe. Ko tembi'u renda ojekuaáva hetave ojejoguahaguére auto-pe, oñepyrũkuri ohechakuaa mba'éichapa oho oguejy yvágare Brandon, Florida-pe, arapokõindy ohasava'ekuépe. Péva oiko rire ohechakuaa rire avei Granbury, Texas, ha Durham, Carolina del Norte-pe, septiembre 2022 guive. Chick-fil-A he'i oĩha hikuái oñepyrũvo ohechakuaa mba'éichapa oho oguejy yvágare hetave tembi'u rendápe. Florida-pe, tapichakuéra ikatúva ojogua ikatu ojapo upéva Chick-fil-A aplicación rupive. Tembi'u oĝuahẽ peteĩ ka'ápe, ojeguerúva ogapýpe peteĩ yvágare oĩva ári peteĩ alambre rupive. Ko empresa omba'apo joaju DroneUp ndive, peteĩ empresa Virginia Beach-gua omba'apóva avei Walmart ndive. Oguejy yvágare ojekuaave ohóvo Estados Unidos-pe, empresa-kuéra Flytrexicha, peteĩ servicio de entrega rápida yvágare rupive, omba'apóva heta tembi'u renda ndive, umíva apytépe Chick-fil-A Texas ha Carolina del Norte-pe septiembre 2022 guive. Oguejy yvágare-gui ndaha'éi, Chick-fil-A ohechakuaávo ambue tecnología autónoma-kuéra, oguejy robot-icha, California, Texas ha Florida-pe. Texas-pe, peteĩ tembi'u renda oiporukuaa peteĩ robot ogueraha hag̃ua tembi'u tapichakuérape oguapývape.'

article_content: 'When protests arose in Tunisia and Egypt early in 2011, Jabbar Savalan, a 19-year-old history student in Azerbaijan, felt inspired. Following the example of activists in the Arab world, he used Facebook to call for a 'Day of Rage' against Azerbaijan's government.  He was arrested on February 5th, according to Amnesty International, and has been in custody since.  Amnesty reports that he was interrogated for two days before seeing a lawyer, allegedly slapped, and pressured to sign a confession. Police claim to have found marijuana in his possession. Despite a blood test showing no trace of drugs and testimony supporting his non-drug use, Savalan was sentenced to prison three months after his arrest, with a release date of August 2013. Amnesty International considers Savalan one of at least 17 'prisoners of conscience' in Azerbaijan. In a report released Wednesday, they accuse the country of suppressing dissent and press freedom, noting increased self-censorship and punishment for criticizing the state. Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev's government employs authoritarian tactics, according to a senior Amnesty official. John Dulhuisen, deputy director of Amnesty's Europe and Central Asia program, stated that opposition groups are allowed to exist but not to function effectively. Amnesty also highlighted the case of Eynulla Fetullayev, a journalist who was imprisoned for four years before his release earlier in 2011.  The Azerbaijani government rejected the report.  Foreign Ministry spokesman Elman Abdullayev said the report was unfair and that media in the country are free.  He denied the existence of prisoners of conscience.  Azerbaijan holds strategic importance due to its oil and gas pipelines that transit to the West. Amnesty suggests that the international community prioritizes these resources over human rights in the country.'
translated_content: 'Amo 2011 oñepyrũvo, Túnez ha Egipto-pe oiko raka’e ojerure haguã mba’e porãve, ha upéva omokyre’ỹ Jabbar Savalan-pe, peteĩ temimbo’e Historia rehegua, 19 áño orekóva, Azerbaiyán-gua. Umi activista árabe-icha, Savalan oipurúkuri Facebook ohenói haguã peteĩ 'Ara Py’a Ro’ysã’ Azerbaiyán retã sãmbyhy rehe. Ojearesókuri chupe 5 jasykõi árape, Amnistía Internacional he’iháicha, ha upégui oĩma preso. Amnistía Internacional omombe’u oñeporandúkuriha chupe mokõi ára pukukue ohecha mboyve ijavokádope, ha upéi oinupã ha ojejopy chupe ohai haguã peteĩ kuatia he’íva ojapohague ivaíva. Policía he’i ojuhúkuri marihuana ijaópe. Savalan oñekondena kuri karáipe mbohapy jasy ojejapo rire hese upe mba’e vaiete, jepémo peteĩ análisis de sangre ohechauka ndaipórihague mba’eve ivaíva hetepýpe, ha ifamília ha iñirũnguéra he’i hague ndoiporúiha mba’eve ivaíva. Osẽta karáigui agosto 2013-pe. Amnistía Internacional he’i Savalan ha’eha peteĩva umi 17 'preso de consciencia’-gui Azerbaiyán-pe. Peteĩ marandu oguenohẽva’ekue ko’ẽme, Amnistía Internacional he’i Azerbaiyán retã ombotyhague umi tapicha ojerurévape mba’e porãve ha avei prensa-pe. He’i avei hetaitereiha umi tapicha okyhyjéva he’i haguã ivaíva retã sãmbyhy rehe. Umi mburuvicha hembiapo vai, he’i peteĩ mburuvicha Amnistía Internacional-gua. John Dulhuisen, Amnistía Internacional Europa ha Asia Central-pegua, he’i oĩha tapicha ojeruréva mba’e porãve, péro ndaikatúiha omba’apo porã. Amnistía Internacional omombe’u avei Eynulla Fetullayev rehe, peteĩ periodista oĩva’ekue preso irundy áño pukukue ojepoi mboyve ko’áĝaite. Azerbaiyán retã sãmbyhy he’i pe marandu ndaha’eiha añetegua. Elman Abdullayev, retã ruvicha, he’i pe marandu ndaha’eiha tekojoja ha prensa ikatúha he’i ojaposéva. He’i ndaiporiha 'preso de consciencia' Azerbaiyán-pe. Ko tetã iñimportanteitereíva petróleo ha gas rehe. Amnistía Internacional he’i umi tetã ambue ohechavéva upe mba’ére ha ndaha’éi umi tapicha rekovére.'

article_content: A disturbing video circulating online, allegedly depicting a Marine throwing a puppy from a cliff, is currently under investigation by the military.  The video, which was removed from YouTube for terms of service violations, shows a small, black-and-white puppy falling through the air accompanied by a yelp.  One person off-camera can be heard saying, 'That's mean, that was mean,' seemingly addressing the alleged perpetrator by his last name.  The video and online discussions identify the Marine as a lance corporal stationed at Marine Corps Base Hawaii in Kaneohe. While his location in the video isn't confirmed, he and another Marine appear to be wearing full combat gear, including helmets.  Marine Corps spokesman Maj. Chris Perrine addressed the video, calling it 'shocking and deplorable' and 'contrary to the high standards' expected of Marines. He assured the public that a thorough investigation is underway and appropriate action will be taken. The Marine's safety is being ensured due to public anger surrounding the incident.  Perrine also highlighted that most Marines behave honorably, citing examples of those who adopt pets from war zones.  If the video is verified, the Marine could face charges ranging from reduction in rank and pay to confinement or even discharge under the Uniform Code of Military Justice. Any other individuals involved will also face disciplinary measures. Perrine acknowledged widespread outrage and emphasized that all Marines are upset by the video, expressing hope that the situation isn't as it appears.

article_content: 'Early Friday morning in Philadelphia's Center City, 22-year-old Amir Bey engaged in a standoff with police, firing a rifle at vehicles and the Masonic Temple.  Authorities responded to reports of gunfire near City Hall, shutting down roads and public transportation.  Police Commissioner Charles Ramsey stated that as the SWAT team arrived, Bey fired at officers, who then returned fire, hitting him multiple times.  Bey was taken to Hahnemann University Hospital in critical condition. Deputy Commissioner Kevin Bethel suggested Bey might have been attempting 'suicide by cop.'  The incident marks the second police-involved shooting that week, adding to the city's increasing homicide count, which has reached 188, exceeding the previous year's total. This incident follows another just days prior during Fourth of July celebrations where police shot a teenager who had shot two others. The area around the Masonic Temple was closed for seven hours as part of the ongoing investigation. No other injuries were reported in Friday's incident.'

Mburuvichakuéra oho upépe ohendu rire oĩha peteĩ kuimba'e ombokapúva hese imboka Municipalidad ypýpe, ombotykuévo tape ha transporte público. Komisario Charles Ramsey omombe'u SWAT equipo og̃uahẽvo, Bey ombokapu hese imboka umi polisía-pe, ha'ekuéra katu ombohovái ichupe, ombokapúvo hese heta jey. Bey ojegueraha Hahnemann Universidad Hospital-pe, oĩháme estado crítico-pe. Komisario Kevin Bethel he'i Bey oiméne oha'ãrõkuri omanomba polisía pópe. Ko mba'e vaiete ha'e mokõiha polisía ojapóva ko arapokõindy ohasávape, ojoapytévo Filadelfiapegua tasa de homicidio ohupytýva 188-pe, hetave ary ohasava'ekuégui. Umi mba'yrumýi Masónico Templo jerére oñemboty 7 aravo pukukue, ojejapo haguére investigación.'

article_content: 'Robert Strauss, a prominent figure in the Democratic Party, passed away Wednesday at the age of 95, according to his law firm.  Strauss led the Democratic National Committee following George McGovern's significant loss to Richard Nixon in the 1972 presidential election and oversaw the party through Jimmy Carter's victory in 1976. He later served as a special trade representative and envoy to the Middle East under President Carter.  Under President George H.W. Bush, a Republican, Strauss served as ambassador to the Soviet Union just prior to its dissolution, and subsequently to Russia.  President Barack Obama praised Strauss, stating, 'Bob was one of the greatest leaders the Democratic Party ever had, and presidents of both parties sought his counsel. He had incredible instincts and a deep passion for public service, not to mention a sharp sense of humor.' Obama's statement, released by the White House, added,  'Bob was truly unique, and our thoughts are with his children, his family, and his many friends.'  CNN's Dana Davidsen and Kevin Bohn contributed to this report.'

Strauss oisãmbyhýkuri Comité Nacional Demócrata George McGovern perdé rire ñepyrũrãme Richard Nixon ndive 1972-pe, ha omyakãkuri pe partido Jimmy Carter ipu'aka peve 1976-pe. Upe rire omba'apókuri embajador ramo Medio Oriente-pe ha representante comercial ramo presidente Carter poguýpe.  Presidente republicano George H. W. Bush poguýpe katu, Strauss omba'apókuri embajador ramo Unión Soviética-pe, oñembovopa rire, ha upe rire Rusia-pe.  Presidente Barack Obama omomba'eguasu Strauss-pe he'ívo: 'Bob ha'ékuri peteĩva umi tendota tuichavévagui Partido Demócrata rembiasápe, ha mokõive partido presidentekuéra ojerure iñe'ẽrendu ha ipy'arory. Oreko va'ekue py'aguasukuéra ijojaha'ỹva ha kyre'ỹ omba'apo hağua tetã rayhupápe, ha hi'ãngatu porãiterei avei.' Obama he'íkuri avei Casa Blanca-gui: 'Bob ha'ékuri peteĩ karai ijojaha'ỹva, ha ñane ñe'ã oĩ imembykuéra, hogayguakuéra ha iñangirũnguéra hetaitéva ndive.'  CNN-pegua Dana Davidsen ha Kevin Bohn oipytyvõkuri ko marandu ñembosako'ípe.'

article_content: 'Following a raid on the home of his chief fundraiser, New York City Mayor Eric Adams vehemently denied any personal involvement in illicit campaign financing on Friday. While professing outrage at any potential misuse of his campaign, Adams committed to a thorough internal review of campaign finances.  Federal agents searched the Brooklyn residence of Brianna Suggs, Adams' primary fundraiser, prompting the mayor to abruptly return to New York, foregoing a scheduled meeting at the White House.  Although declining comment, the US Attorney's office in Manhattan is reportedly investigating possible collusion between the Adams campaign and the Turkish government to secure illegal foreign contributions, according to The New York Times.  The search warrant reportedly targeted records pertaining to campaign contributions, travel to Turkiye by campaign affiliates, and communications between the campaign and Turkish officials.  Adams emphatically stated he was unaware of any inappropriate fundraising practices, particularly involving foreign funds. KSK Construction Group and a small university in Washington, D.C., both with ties to the Turkish government, are also named in the warrant.  While Suggs has not been charged, campaign records reveal over $13,000 in donations from individuals listing KSK Construction as their employer. Several of these individuals declined comment when contacted, with some indicating they were advised against public statements. At least one donor confirmed being contacted by federal authorities.  Adams has publicly acknowledged his relationship with Turkiye, stemming from numerous visits during his time as a state senator and Brooklyn borough president.  This federal inquiry follows other investigations into connections between Adams' inner circle and New York's real estate industry, including bribery and straw donor allegations against former city officials and associates.  While Adams has not been personally implicated in these cases, the current investigation targeting his top fundraising staff raises concerns among political analysts.'
translated_content: 'Oikóvo peteĩ jejopy vaípe ojejapohague hógape ijyvykuéra apytégui viru ombyatýva pegua, Nueva York táva pegua karai guasu Eric Adams oñembohovái mbaretépe oĩhaguéicha oikuaa upe mba'e vaígui viernes pyharevépe.  Omombe'úvo ipochyetereíha oiméramo ojejapohague vyrorei iñemongu'erãme, karai guasu Adams he'i ojehesarekotaha opa mba'e ojejapohague viru ñembyatýpe. Agente federal-kuéra oike hikuái Brianna Suggs rógape, Brooklyn-pe, ha'éva karai guasu viru ombyatýva tenondegua, upévare karai guasu ou jey Nueva York-pe, ndohóigui peteĩ aty guasúpe Casa Blanca-pe. Jepe ndoikuaaséi mba'eve, FISCALÍA Manhattan-pegua ohecha oimépa vyrorei ojejapohague karai guasu rembiguái ha gobierno turco ndive, he'iháicha kuatiañe'ẽ The New York Times.  Ojeheka kuatia oĩva viru ñembyatýre, viaje Turquía-pe ha gobierno turco ndive ñomongeta. Adams he'i ndoikuaaiha mba'evete vyrorei rehegua.  KSK Construcción ha peteĩ mbo'ehaovusu Washington D.C.-pe, ojoajuha gobierno turco ndive, oĩ avei upe ojehekávape.  Suggs ndojeguerahavéi ka'irãime, viru ñembyatýpe ojehecha USD 13.000 rupi oñeme'ẽhague KSK Construcción-gui. Heta umívagui ndoikuaaséi mba'eve. Ko mba'e oikóva rire ojeheka ambue mba'e ojejapóva Adams-pegua ha omba'apóva Nueva York róga apoha ndive.'

article_content: 'In a move towards greater fairness, the Department of Defense, under then-Secretary Robert Gates, announced modifications to the 'don't ask, don't tell' policy in 2010. This policy, enacted in 1993, restricted open homosexual service in the military. The changes, effective within 30 days, focused on raising the bar for investigations into alleged homosexual conduct.  Gates emphasized that these adjustments reflected 'common sense' and 'common decency,' stemming from 17 years of experience with the policy. Key changes included elevating the authority to initiate inquiries and separations to general or flag officers, demanding stricter standards for credible information (like requiring sworn statements instead of hearsay), and protecting confidential communications with lawyers, clergy, and therapists.  President Obama and Admiral Mike Mullen, then-Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, supported a full legislative repeal, while some senior military officials voiced apprehension about potential impacts on unit cohesion.  Gates acknowledged these concerns and aimed to minimize disruption during the transition. He also commissioned the RAND Corporation to update its 1993 study on the effects of allowing open homosexual service.  Over 13,500 service members were discharged under the policy since its inception, with the lowest rate in 2009. Public opinion shifted considerably from 1994, with a significant increase in support for allowing openly gay people to serve.  This move signaled a shift in military policy and sparked ongoing discussions about inclusivity and equality in the armed forces.'

Ko rembipotápe, oñemoĩva'ekue 1993-pe, ojoko kuimba'e térã kuña ojohayhúva ojuehe omba'apo peve ñemihápe. Umi ñemoambue, oñemomba'eguasútava 30 ára rire, oñecentra ñeporandu ñemopu'ãme kuimba'e térã kuña ojohayhúva ojuehe rembiapo vai rehe. Gates omyesakãkuri ko'ã ñemyatyrõ ohechaukaha \'akã porã\' ha \'teko marangatu\', oúva 17 ary ojeipurúvo ko rembipotápe. Mba'e guasuete oñemoambueva'ekue ha'e hína mburuvicha guasu térã yvateve oñeme'ẽvaicha chupekuéra pu'aka ñeporandu ha ñemosẽ hag̃ua, jerure hekopeteve marandu añetegua rehe (ojerurévo ñe'ẽme'ẽ mymba jurúpe ñe'ẽ reity ypykuévo), ha oñangarekóvo marandu ñemime'ẽ rehe avogádo, pa'i ha pohanohára ndive. Mburuvicha Guasu Obama ha almirante Mike Mullen, tendota Mburuvicha Joajuha Ruvicha, omoirũkuri ñembope'a guasu, heta mburuvicha ruvicha yvate ohechaukáramo kyhyje oguerukuaa rehe ñañemoirũme. Gates ohechakuaa ko'ã kyhyje ha oipota'ỹre ñemongu'e pe ñemoambue aja. Avei ojerure RAND Atýpe omoambue hag̃ua iñemoarandu 1993 pegua kuimba'e térã kuña ojohayhúva ojuehe omba'apokuaa rehe ñemihápe. 13.500 rupi oĩva ñemihápe oñemosẽkuri ko rembipotápe oñemopyenda guive, iporãvéva 2009-pe. Tekoha rayhupápe tuicha ñemoambue oiko 1994 guive, hetavéva oguerohorývo kuimba'e térã kuña ojohayhúva ojuehe omba'apokuaa ñemihápe. Ko tembiapo ohechauka ñemoambue ñemihápe rembipotápe ha ñomongeta opave'ỹva teko potĩ ha joja rehe ñemihápe.'

article_content: 'The death of Ronald Singleton, 45, while in police custody in Manhattan on July 13, has been ruled a homicide. The medical examiner cited 'physical restraint by police during excited delirium due to acute phencyclidine (PCP) intoxication' as the cause.  This incident preceded the death of Eric Garner by four days, which garnered national attention due to the officer's use of a chokehold. Singleton was detained after a taxi driver reported his erratic behavior near St. Patrick's Cathedral. According to reports, a struggle ensued during the arrest, and Singleton went into cardiac arrest while being transported to Roosevelt Hospital. Contributing factors to his death included hypertensive and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and obesity. The NYPD is cooperating with the Manhattan district attorney's investigation.'
translated_content: 'Ronald Singleton, 45, omano rire Manhattan, 13 jasypokõi me, oje'e ojuká ramo hague. Mba'ejerure oikuaauká 'py'amongetá polisía reheve excited delirium-pe, PCP intoxilación reheve' ha'ehague pe ojukáva. Ko mba'e oiko Eric Garner mano mboyve irundy ára, peteĩ káso oipy'apýva opavavépe chokehold polisía oiporuva'ekuére. Singleton ojeapresa rire peteĩ taxista he'i hague heko ky'a haguére Catedral de San Patricio ypýpe. Oje'e oñorairõ hague ojeapresárõ guare, ha upéi Singleton py'amongueta ijetu'u ohóvo Roosevelt Hospital-pe. Hi'ymba, hi'aheta, ha ñepohano heta oipytyvõ avei omanó haguã. Polisía Nueva York-gua omba'apo hína fiscalía ndive ko káso rehe.'
post_content: 'Man's death in NYPD custody ruled homicide.  This case, occurring before Eric Garner's, raises serious questions about police use of force. #PoliceBrutality #JusticeForSingleton #NYPD'

article_content: 'During a visit to the Romanian parliament, House of Commons Speaker John Bercow generated controversy by stating that Eastern European migrants often demonstrate a stronger work ethic than some British workers.  He praised the 'important wave' of migrants who have come to Britain in recent years, emphasizing their skills and dedication.  These remarks sparked criticism due to the expectation of political neutrality associated with the Speaker's role.  Nigel Farage, leader of the UK Independence Party, called Bercow's actions 'disgraceful,' questioning his disregard for the traditionally neutral stance of the Speaker.  Bercow defended his statement, asserting his right to express his views and highlighting the benefits of immigration.  He also criticized media coverage of immigration, suggesting a negative bias.  Conservative MPs expressed differing opinions, with some condemning Bercow's perceived breach of neutrality while others defended his freedom of speech.  This incident underscores the ongoing debate regarding the balance between political neutrality, freedom of expression, and sensitive political issues like immigration.'
translated_content: 'Oguahẽvo Parlamento Rumania-pe, pe Speaker Cámara de los Comunes-gua, John Bercow, omoheñói ñe’ẽmeguasu he’ívo umi inmigrante Europa del Este-gua omba’apo mbaretevehague omba’apóvagui Gran Bretaña-pe. Oguerohory ‘ola mboypy’ inmigrante ouva’ekue Gran Bretaña-pe ko’ã arýpe, ohechaukávo imba’ekuaaita ha hembi’apokuaa. Ko’ã ñe’ẽ omoheñói ñe’ẽpohýi pe neutralidad política oñeha’arõvagui pe Speaker-gui. Nigel Farage, líder Partido de la Independencia del Reino Unido-gua, he’i Bercow rembiapo ‘oñembohorýiha’, ombojovakévo pe neutralidad ojeha’arõva chugui. Bercow oñedefende he’ívo iderechoha he’i haguã hemimo’ã ha ohechaukávo inmigración mba’eporã. Okritika avei umi medio de comunicación he’íva inmigración rehe, ohechaukávo peteĩ lado negativo. Umi parlamentario conservador he’i opáichagua mba’e, oĩ okritikáva Bercow neutralidad rehe ha oĩ odefendeva’ekue iderecho he’i haguã hemimo’ã. Ko mba’e ohechauka pe debate neutralidad política, libertad de expresión ha tema delicado inmigración rehegua.'

article_content: 'Bollywood actress Tabu, celebrating her 52nd birthday, demonstrates that age is no barrier to defying societal expectations and embracing a fulfilling single life. In a recent Hindustan Times Brunch interview, she expressed contentment with her single status, rejecting the negativity often associated with it. Tabu emphasized that happiness stems from various sources unrelated to romantic relationships and highlighted the importance of self-acceptance.  She firmly believes that sacrificing her acting career and passion for travel for a partner would have been a disservice to herself.  Her ideal relationship prioritizes mutual personal growth and liberation, not restrictive constraints. While open to love and marriage throughout her life, Tabu hasn't felt pressured to pursue either.  She acknowledges the evolving complexities of relationships and values individual experiences and independence.  She views individuals as unique entities, moving beyond traditional gender roles.  Tabu candidly shared that she considered having a child outside of marriage but ultimately decided against it, prioritizing the child's well-being.  Continuing her successful acting career, Tabu is set to appear in 'Auron Mein Kahan Dum Tha' and 'The Crew,' alongside Kriti Sanon and Kareena Kapoor.'

Peteĩ ñomongeta ramo Hindustan Times Brunch ndive, ha'e he'i ovy'aha oikóvo ha'eño ha ohechauka ndaha'éiha mba'e vaiete. Tabu he'i vy'a ouha heta mba'égui ha ndaha'éiha peteĩ kuimba'e reheguánte. Ha'e oguerovia ojapo vaietehague ohejáramo hembiapo ha iviaha tekoayhu rehehápe. Ikatu ohayhu ha omenda, Tabu ndojapói upéva ojeipy'ara'ỹre. Ha'e omomba'e opavavéva reko ha isãso. Omombe'u avei oimo'ãhague imemby ha'eño ha upéi ndojaposéi oñangareko rupi mitãre. Tabu osegíta hembiapo ha oĩta 'Auron Mein Kahan Dum Tha' ha 'The Crew'-pe, Kriti Sanon ha Kareena Kapoor ndive.'

article_content: 'Migrants hiding in food lorries entering the UK are threatening fresh food supplies. If a migrant is found, entire truckloads of imported produce are destroyed, potentially leading to shortages or price increases. Home Secretary Theresa May is meeting with the food industry to address this issue. Migrants board lorries as far away as Spain, and current detection methods at points of entry like Calais or within the UK result in cargo destruction.  The release of apprehended migrants by French authorities enables them to make further attempts to enter the UK, often by hiding in food lorries, which exacerbates the food waste problem. The UK Border Force employs sniffer dogs, CO2 detectors, heartbeat monitors, scanners, and visual searches to find stowaways. This situation, along with the destruction of contaminated goods, has raised concerns within the retail sector about the potential impact on fresh food supplies.'

Ministra del Interior, Theresa May, oñomongeta hína umi tembi’u apoha ndive ko apañu’ũ ñembohovái haguã. article_content: 'Tottenham showed resilience in a hard-fought 2-1 win over Swansea City. Christian Eriksen's late goal in the 89th minute sealed the victory for Spurs, echoing his last-gasp winner against Hull City. Manager Mauricio Pochettino commended his side's fighting spirit, highlighting the team's increasing adoption of his tactical approach.  Eriksen's vital contribution came after Harry Kane's early header gave Tottenham the lead. Swansea's Wilfried Bony equalized in the second half, but Spurs ultimately prevailed.  Despite Swansea creating numerous chances, Pochettino believed his team deserved the win. Meanwhile, Swansea manager Garry Monk expressed frustration, attributing the defeat to individual errors and a lack of clinical finishing.  He also questioned certain refereeing decisions, notably involving Spurs' Erik Lamela, though maintained these were not the sole reason for the loss.'

Idirek Mauricio Pochettino omomba'e hembireko mbarete ha he'i equipo oipuru porãveha ikatupyryha. Eriksen rembiapo ou rire peteĩ gol Harry Kane-gui iñepyrũme. Swansea Wilfried Bony omoĩ peteĩ gol jepiguáicha, ha Spurs ogana upe rire. Jepe Swansea ojapo heta mba'e porã, Pochettino he'i equipo omereseha ipu'aka. Upe aja, Swansea idirek Garry Monk oñe'ẽpochy, he'ívo ikane'õhaguére ha hembireko ndojapói porãhaguére. Omombe'u avei arbitro rembiapo, oñe'ẽ Erik Lamela rehe, jepémo he'i ndaha'éiha upéva ikane'õhaguére.'

article_content: 'David Ainsworth, the 49-year-old Deputy Chief Constable of Wiltshire Police, tragically took his own life amidst an investigation into claims of sexual harassment against female colleagues.  A coroner confirmed his death by hanging was suicide. Ainsworth, earning \u00a3110,000 a year, was reportedly distressed by the accusations, fearing the loss of his career and reputation.  Around a dozen staff members, primarily women, had come forward with a total of 27 allegations regarding inappropriate conduct. One reported incident involved a comment about a female colleague's buttons.  Despite his anxiety, professional assessments did not identify any immediate risk to his life. While Ainsworth had not faced criminal charges, disciplinary action was a possibility.  Wiltshire Police Authority Chairman Chris Hoare expressed condolences to Ainsworth's family and confirmed the ongoing nature of the investigation, emphasizing support for the individuals who reported the allegations. Ainsworth's estranged wife described him as a 'shell' of his former self, drastically changed by the accusations.  His partner, Jo Howes, discovered his body. The coroner's verdict was suicide.'

Peteĩ juez ohechakuaákuri ijupekuereihague oñembo'yha. Ainsworth, hembiapópe £110,000 opáguinte ary, oñeñandu vaieterei umi mba'e oje'évare hese, okyhyjégui imba'apo ha iñe'ẽporãve ohundi.  Amo peteĩ docena funcionaria, hetave kuña, he'i hesekuéra ojapohague mba'e naiporãiva. Peteĩva he'i hese ohechareihague ibotón kuñakarai rembiapokue. Oiméne oñekevrantaitereíramo jepe, umi profesional nohechakuaái mba'eveichagua peligro oikotevẽva oñeñatende porãve. Ainsworth ndoikéi ka'irãime, jepémo ikatúkuri oñekastiga chupe imba'apópe. Wiltshire Policíapegua tendota guasu, Chris Hoare, omombe'u ipy'arasy Ainsworth rogayguakuérape ha ohechauka investigación ohoha gueteri, oipytyvõvo umi kuñanguérape oñe'ẽva'ekue hese. Hembireko ymaguare he'i ha'ehague peteĩ 'kuimba'e nandi'ỹva', tuichaiterei okambiáva umi mba'e oje'éva hese rupi. Iparja'i, Jo Howes, otopa ikangue. Juez he'i ojejukahague.'

article_content: Forty-two years after the tragic Kent State shootings, the Justice Department has decided against reopening the investigation.  The decision follows the review of digitally enhanced audio recordings submitted by Alan Canfora, a wounded survivor, who believes they contain evidence of an order to fire given to the Ohio National Guard before they shot student protestors in 1970.  Four students died, and nine were injured during the protest against the Vietnam War and the U.S. invasion of Cambodia. While Canfora maintains an independent audio analysis supports his claim, the Justice Department found the recording inconclusive.  Assistant U.S. Attorney General Thomas Perez stated that the audio quality was poor, and no clear command could be discerned.  Furthermore, the statute of limitations prevents legal action. Despite the legal roadblocks, Canfora emphasized his desire for truth and a historical acknowledgment of what happened rather than a retrial. He and other victims' families feel a lack of closure due to the unresolved questions surrounding the tragic event. They now plan to pursue the case in an international court.

Ko decisión ou ojehecha rire umi grabación de audio omohenda porãvéva digitalmente, ome'ẽva'ekue Alan Canfora, peteĩ sobreviviente ojeheriva'ekue, ogueroviáva oĩha ipype prueba oñeme'ẽhague orden oñedispara haguã Guardia Nacional de Ohio-pe odispara mboyve umi estudiante oprotestávape 1970-pe. Irundy estudiante omano, ha poteĩ ojeherni ko protesta aja Guerra del Vietnam ha invasión estadounidense Camboya-pe rehe. Canfora he'i peteĩ análisis de audio independiente oapojaha iñe'ẽ, pe Departamento de Justicia he'i pe grabación ndojekuaái porãha. Pe Fiscal General Adjunto Thomas Perez he'i pe audio ikalidad ivaietereiha, ha ndojekuaái porãiha mba'eveichagua orden. Avei, pe estatuto de limitaciones ojoko ojejapo haguã acción legal. Jepémo oĩ umi mba'e ojokóva legalmente, Canfora he'i ohekáha añetegua ha jehechakuaa histórico upe mba'e oikova'ekue rehe, ndaha'éi peteĩ nuevo juicio. Ha'e ha umi familia víctima-kuéra oñandu hikuái ndohechakuaaporãiha opa mba'e ko mba'e vaiete rehe. Ko'ágã oplanea ohupyty justicia peteĩ corte internacional-pe.
